freshly_checked_applications.status: Published theorem; all application hypotheses checked in GLS8
freshly_checked_applications.author: W. Banaszczyk
freshly_checked_applications.title: New bounds in some transference theorems in the geometry of numbers
freshly_checked_applications.primary_text_retrieval: Original paper transcription, section 2, Theorem (2.1), printed p.631; publisher metadata independently checked. The primary text includes the n=1 equality case.
freshly_checked_applications.statement_used: For every full Euclidean lattice M in R^n, λ_i(M) λ_{n+1−i}(M*) ≤ n; only i=n is used.
hypothesis_match: M is the original Hermitian dual L_c^vee embedded in S tensor_Q R; n=[E:Q]k.
B(x,y)=Tr_{E/Q} h_S(x,y) is real symmetric positive definite, by CM trace invariance and original ColVal positivity.
L_c^vee is a full finitely generated Z-lattice, hence discrete and spans the Euclidean space.
Integer-pairing dual M* is exactly D_E^(-1)L_c, with no factor two in B.
For nonzero z in M*, h(z,z) lies in D_E^(-2); ideal norm and AM–GM give λ_1(M*) ≥ sqrt([E:Q])/rd(E).
Result gives k E-independent y_a in the original L_c^vee with Tr h(y_a,y_a)/(2f) ≤ k^2(2v)^2.
freshly_checked_applications.not_claimed: The chapter does not reconstruct Banaszczyk's Gaussian transference proof; this is an explicit category A import.
freshly_checked_applications.application_scope: Any original ColVal D u and any original level-zero class c, before family, word, or place thresholds are introduced.
original_source_facts: ColVal supplies the original full class lattice L_c, its positive definite Hermitian form, and LatT integrality.
The original host has [E:Q]=2f and v=rd(E)/2; no redefinition of either normalization is made.
The target ShortAt bound is Tr h(y_a,y_a)/(2f) <= k^2(2v)^2 for k E-independent vectors in L_c^vee.
independently_derived_normalization: For B=Tr h the integer-pairing dual of L_c^vee is D_E^(-1)L_c, since h is Hermitian and the codifferent is stable under CM conjugation.
If z is nonzero in that trace dual, beta=h(z,z) is totally positive and belongs to D_E^(-2); therefore |Norm beta| disc(E)^2 >= 1.
AM–GM gives B(z,z)>= [E:Q]/rd(E)^2, and hence lambda_1(M*)>=sqrt([E:Q])/rd(E).
The published inequality in dimension n=[E:Q]k gives lambda_n(M)^2 <= [E:Q] k^2 rd(E)^2.
Extracting k E-independent vectors and dividing by [E:Q]=2f yields the exact source target, with rd(E)=2v and no extra factor two or T.

note: New direct A application: Banaszczyk 1993 Thm2.1 on the exact positive trace Euclidean lattice; its normalization and subsequent transports are proved in GLS. Earlier A applications retain their exact scopes.
